If you fired a bullet straight at a sword's edge,
you'd expect the blade to shatter.
But most bullets are soft lead,
wrapped in a thin copper jacket.
And a katana's edge is hardened steel,
So when they meet, the blade doesn't break.
It slices the bullet clean in two!
And the halves fly off either side.
But no one can react to a real bullet.
The sword has to be waiting, right in its path!
